answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Proof of unique rally co-driver record flips the bet — stage results recorded over two seasons — and the dawn lands on the attacker instead. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that stage results recorded over two seasons — so privacy survives, and the meadow is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The whisper grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
